chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding a woman who cut off the breast of her slave girl: 'She is free, there is no way for her mistress upon her.' And he judged regarding the one who tortured his slave: 'So he is free, there is no way for him upon him. He is a Sa'iba (unconditionally free), he can go and give his mastership to the one he likes. So when he takes the responsibility of his crimes, he would inherit him.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.سَائِبَة: A slave who becomes free and chooses their own master

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a slave who is mutilated or tortured by their master in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details Imam Ali’s (AS) jurisprudential rulings on manumission due to injury (‘Uqala) and voluntary emancipation (Sa’iba). It establishes that severe mutilation by the owner grants the slave immediate freedom, while a master who tortures his slave loses exclusive ownership rights, allowing the slave to choose a new master and potentially inherit from him upon assuming liability for his crimes.
